edges.effect_quant: Among BRCA1 and BRCA2 carriers, risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy is associated with marked reductions in ovarian cancer events and ovarian cancer-specific mortality. In the large 2010 multicenter prospective cohort, ovarian cancer-specific mortality was lower after surgery with HR 0.21.
edges.population: women carrying pathogenic BRCA1 or BRCA2 variants who undergo preventive bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy before ovarian cancer develops
edges.mechanism: Removal of the ovaries and fallopian tubes substantially reduces the tissue at highest risk for BRCA-associated tubo-ovarian carcinogenesis and therefore lowers downstream ovarian cancer incidence and death.
edges.summary: This is one of the strongest hereditary gynecologic prevention edges in the corpus. The evidence is observational rather than randomized, but across large BRCA carrier cohorts the mortality and risk-reduction signal is consistent enough to support a clearly protective label.
edges.caveats: The intervention induces surgical menopause unless performed after natural menopause, so the decision is highly preference-sensitive and age-dependent. This edge focuses on ovarian cancer mortality and does not encode tradeoffs such as menopausal symptoms, bone loss, cardiovascular effects, or the residual risk of primary peritoneal carcinoma.

evidence.citation: Rebbeck TR et al 2002 N Engl J Med
evidence.notes: Prophylactic oophorectomy in carriers of BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutations.
